newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs track Wall St, recoup losses to end up.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs track Wall St, recoup losses to end up.

text.p: Brazilian shares recouped early losses and ended higher and in a bullish mood, boosted by strong gains on Wall Street and a late surge in benchmark Telebras, brokers said.
"There was profit-taking early on but the market stabilized later and investors with open positions began buying to cover themselves," one broker said.
The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa index of 49 most-traded shares closed up 0.32 percent at 74,783 points on hefty turnover of 633.4 million reais ($608.4 million).

Brokers said shares opened sharply lower in broad profit-taking as investors hedged against an expected drop on Wall Street on the release of U.S. jobs data and on concerns about the new CPMF tax on financial transactions.
But prices bounced back later, shrugging off Brasilia's decision to levy the tax on foreign capital when it enters and leaves Brazil and following the rise in the Dow Jones.

"The reaction to the CPMF rules was less than expected," one dealer said. "Investors apparently are not too concerned about it. They are more interested in re-election and, on that, the market is optimistic."
Congress next week is expected to hold a first round of voting on a constitutional amendment that would allow President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to run for an unprecedented second term in 1998.
The market's late surge was propelled by hikes in Telebras, whose shares and options regularly account for 65 percent of daily bolsa trade.
Telebras' benchmark preferred, which had been down more than one percent at midsession, closed up 0.82 percent at 86.20 reais, while its voting common ended up 0.25 percent at 79.60 reais.
Other telecoms and major blue chips also rose in active late trade. State oil monopoly Petrobras gained 0.29 percent at 178.50 reais while Telebras unit Telesp ended up 0.84 percent at 239.00 reais.

Still, some shares ended lower, despite the market's overall rise. State power firm Eletrobras closed down 1.75 perent 393.00 reais and state mining firm Vale do Rio Doce declined 0.68 percent to end at 21.95 reais.
Despite the drop in Eletrobras, the bolsa's Electrical Energy Index .IEE of nine most-liquid power shares rose 0.78 percent to end at 2,141 points led by a rise in state-owned Eletropaulo.
Eletropaulo preferred climbed 5.88 percent to close at 180 reais after its owner, Sao Paulo state, accepted bids from groups interested in advising on its privatization.
Meanwhile, the market's new and wider Brazil Index (IBX) of 100 leading shares closed 0.41 percent higher to end at 1,625 points.
